blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) provides vital head-to-toe protection against workshop hazards.
Proper selection of PPE requires evaluating specific environmental risks, fit, and regulatory compliance.
Effective hazard management mandates proper training in the correct usage and donning of equipment.
Regular inspection, cleaning, and maintenance are essential to ensure the reliability and longevity of PPE.
PPE serves as the final line of defense and should supplement primary engineering and administrative controls.

blocks.content: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) refers to protective clothing, helmets, gloves, goggles, and other equipment designed to protect workers from injuries and health hazards in workplaces. In technical trades such as fitting, welding, electrical work, and mechanical maintenance, workers are exposed to risks like flying particles, heat, electric shock, noise, and harmful chemicals. PPE acts as a barrier between the worker and these hazards.
PPE does not eliminate hazards completely, but it significantly reduces the chances of injury when used properly along with safe working practices.

items: Protects workers from injuries and accidents
Reduces exposure to harmful substances
Prevents burns, cuts, and eye injuries
Ensures safer working conditions
Improves confidence and productivity of workers

cells: Protects eyes from dust, sparks, and metal particles
Protects entire face from sparks and chemicals
Protects hands from cuts, burns, and chemicals
Protects body from heat, sparks, and chemicals
Protects lungs from dust and harmful gases

blocks.content: The selection of PPE depends on the type of hazard present in the workplace. Proper assessment of risks must be done before choosing protective equipment.

items: PPE should be comfortable and properly fitted
It should provide adequate protection for the specific hazard
It should be durable and easy to maintain
It should meet safety standards and regulations
Always wear PPE before starting work
Ensure PPE is properly fitted
Do not remove PPE while working in hazardous areas
Use PPE according to manufacturer instructions
Replace damaged PPE immediately

cells: PPE should be cleaned after use to remove dust and contaminants
Store PPE in dry and clean places
Check PPE regularly for damage or wear

items: Hierarchy of Hazard Control: Note that PPE is always classified as the final line of defense after engineering controls.
Selection and Maintenance Criteria: Questions often test specific maintenance protocols and criteria for replacing damaged PPE.
Equipment Classification: Frequently tested on matching specific PPE types to corresponding workshop hazards.

blocks.content: Although PPE is essential for safety, it should not be the only method used to control hazards. Engineering controls, machine guards, and proper training should also be used.

items: PPE may not eliminate hazards completely
Improper use reduces effectiveness
Damaged PPE may fail to provide protection
PPE stands for Personal Protective Equipment.
PPE protects workers from workplace hazards.
Common PPE includes helmets, gloves, goggles, safety shoes, and masks.
PPE must be properly maintained and inspected regularly.
